net sales.text: The following is an analysis of sales by market and by region:

Semiconductor.text: We are an innovative manufacturer of semiconductor process equipment. Our proven ion beam, laser annealing, lithography, MOCVD, and single wafer wet processing technologies play an integral role in the fabrication and packaging of advanced semiconductor devices. With equipment designed to optimize performance, yield and cost of ownership, Veeco holds leading technology positions in the markets we serve. To learn more about Veeco’s systems and service offerings, visit www.veeco.com .

Compound Semiconductor.text: Compound Semiconductor revenue increased by 268% in the third quarter from the comparable prior year period, comprising 19% of total revenue. In the Compound Semiconductor market, our broad portfolio of ion beam deposition, wet processing, and MOCVD technologies are gaining momentum as investments in AI data center infrastructure drive demand for higher-speed optical connectivity and more power efficient semiconductor devices.

Data Storage.text: Data Storage market revenue increased by 101% in the third quarter from the comparable prior year period, comprising 10% of total revenue. We address the Data Storage market with sales of our Ion Beam technology and wet process systems driven by demand for cloud and AI data centers. We expect full-year 2026 revenue in this market to approximately double compared to 2025 and have order visibility extending into 2027. We remain engaged with customers on their technology roadmaps, including the adoption of heat-assisted magnetic recording, which is contributing to renewed investment and demand for our technologies.

Scientific & Other.text: Scientific & Other market revenue decreased by 48% in the third quarter from the comparable prior year period, comprising 6% of total revenue. Demand in this market is primarily project-driven and includes sales to government-funded laboratories, universities, research institutions and customers developing emerging technologies. We address the Scientific & Other market with several technologies, including Molecular Beam Epitaxy (“MBE”), Atomic Layer Deposition (“ALD”), MOCVD, Wet Processing, and ion beam deposition and etch systems. These technologies support research, development and specialized production applications across areas such as quantum computing and other advanced materials.

intro.text: Headquartered in Plainview, New York, we were organized as a Delaware corporation in 1989. We are a manufacturer of advanced semiconductor process equipment that solves an array of challenging materials engineering problems for our customers. Our comprehensive collection of ion beam, laser annealing, metal organic chemical vapor deposition (“MOCVD”), chemical vapor deposition (“CVD”), advanced packaging lithography, single wafer wet processing, molecular beam epitaxy (“MBE”), and atomic layer deposition (“ALD”) technologies play an integral role in the fabrication of key devices that are enabling the 4th industrial revolution of all things connected.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Revenue from the sales of parts, upgrades, service, and support represented approximately 25%, 20%, and 22% of our net sales for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024, and 2023, respectively.
Parts and upgrade sales represented approximately 19%, 15%, and 17% of our net sales for those years, respectively, and service and support sales were 6%, 5%, and 5% respectively.
Our net sales to customers located outside of the United States represented approximately 85% of our total net sales in 2025.
Our net sales denominated in currencies other than the U.S. dollar represented approximately 4% of total net sales in 2025.
The Company depends on purchases from its ten largest customers, which accounted for 68 % and 63 % of net accounts receivable at December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Customers who accounted for more than 10% of net accounts receivable or net sales are as follows:
We rely on certain principal customers for a significant portion of our sales.
While we rely on our outsourcing partners to perform their contracted functions, we maintain some level of internal manufacturing capability for these systems.
Our success depends on our ability to attract, retain, and motivate employees.

Our ability to remain competitive depends on our ability to enhance existing products and develop and manufacture new products in a timely and cost effective manner and to accurately predict technology transitions.
To meet these demands, we depend on the timely delivery of parts, components, and subassemblies from our suppliers.

Furthermore, certain key parts may be subject to long lead-times or may be obtainable only from a single supplier or limited group of suppliers, and some sourcing and assembly is provided by suppliers located in countries other than the United States.
We rely on a limited number of suppliers, some of whom are our sole source for particular components.
Certain of the parts, components, and sub-assemblies included in our products are obtained from a single source or a limited group of suppliers.

While we maintain some level of internal manufacturing capability for these systems, we rely on our outsourcing partners to perform their contracted functions to allow us flexibility to adapt to changing market conditions, including periods of significantly diminished order volumes.
The timing of an order often depends on our customer’s capital expenditure budget, over which we have no control.

Significant disruptions in our information technology systems (or those of our key suppliers, contract manufacturers, distributors, sales agents and other partners) or other data security incidents could adversely affect our business operations and result in the loss or misappropriation of, and unauthorized access to, sensitive information.

The realization of net deferred tax assets relies on our ability to generate future taxable income, and, as such, if the Company is unable to generate sufficient future taxable income, we may not obtain the full benefit of these deferred tax assets.

In addition, changes in environmental laws and regulations, including those relating to greenhouse gas emissions and other climate change matters, could require us (and/or our key suppliers, contract manufacturers and other partners) to install new equipment, alter operations to incorporate new technologies, or implement new processes, among other measures, which may cause us to incur significant costs and divert management attention.
While the Company relies on its outsourcing partners to perform their contracted functions, the Company maintains some level of internal manufacturing capability for these systems.
In addition, certain of the components and sub-assemblies included in the Company’s products are obtained from a single source or a limited group of suppliers.
